matchstick.title: V↔X transformation via single stick reposition
matchstick.principle: A V (two diagonal sticks) can be turned into an X (two crossing diagonals) by moving one of its sticks, and vice‑versa, changing the numeral’s value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a V or X appears and the numeric discrepancy suggests a change of exactly five.
matchstick.example: Turn V (5) into X (10) by moving one diagonal to cross the other.

matchstick.title: Check numeric discrepancy to guide stick moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the integer values of both sides of the equation; the difference indicates how much the total must change, guiding which numeral or operator to modify.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, after translating the Roman numerals to integers.
matchstick.example: If left side is 2 and right side 25, the discrepancy is 23, suggesting a large value change is needed.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign integrity
matchstick.principle: The ‘=’ sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; moving a stick from or to it would invalidate the operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever considering a stick move, never involve the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Do not take a horizontal stick from ‘=’ to turn a numeral into a different shape.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters after move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, each numeral and operator must still be a recognizable Roman numeral or valid arithmetic symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing a stick move, check every character’s shape against the allowed set.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from ‘+’ to form an ‘I’ must leave ‘+’ as a valid ‘-’ sign.

matchstick.title: Consider intra‑character stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved within the same character, effectively reshaping it (e.g., turning a V into an X by repositioning a diagonal).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single character’s value needs to change without affecting other characters.
matchstick.example: Shift one diagonal of a V to cross the other, creating an X.

matchstick.title: Avoid orientation mismatches
matchstick.principle: Sticks retain their orientation; a vertical stick cannot become diagonal, and a horizontal cannot become vertical.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick, ensure the destination shape requires the same orientation.
matchstick.example: A vertical stick from ‘+’ can be placed only where a vertical line is needed, such as forming an ‘I’.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion only when resulting operator is valid
matchstick.principle: Changing an operator (e.g., ‘+’ to ‘-’) must leave both the original and new operator as valid symbols, using stick moves that respect their definitions.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the arithmetic operation needs to change to balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Remove the vertical stick from ‘+’ to turn it into ‘-’, and use that stick elsewhere.

matchstick.title: Recompute numeric values after transformation
matchstick.principle: After any candidate stick move, recalculate the Roman‑numeral values to verify that the equality now holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each proposed move, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: After turning ‘+’ into ‘-’ and adding a stick to form ‘III’, compute 3 = 14 - 11.

matchstick.title: Plus‑to‑minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; moving the vertical stick away turns it into a minus sign, and the moved stick can be used to form or extend another numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy suggests that changing addition to subtraction would reduce the right‑hand total, and a vertical stick is available from the plus sign.
matchstick.example: Move the vertical stick from ‘+’ to the left side ‘II’, turning ‘+’ into ‘-’ and ‘II’ into ‘III’.

matchstick.title: Dual‑character stick relocation for balancing values
matchstick.principle: Moving a stick from one character to another simultaneously changes both characters’ values; use this to offset the numeric discrepancy in a single move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the required change in total value can be achieved by decreasing one character’s value and increasing another’s by the same amount.
matchstick.example: Take a vertical stick from ‘+’ (reducing it to ‘-’) and add it to ‘II’ (making ‘III’), balancing 3 = 14 - 11.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as interchangeable pieces, ignoring that a vertical stick cannot become diagonal or horizontal without rotation, which is prohibited.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always keep the original orientation of a stick; only relocate it to a position that requires the same orientation.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may think moving a stick from ‘=’ can help balance the equation, overlooking the rule that ‘=’ must stay as two horizontal sticks.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never consider any stick move that adds to or removes from the ‘=’ sign; treat it as immutable.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid character after move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on numeric balance and forgets that each character must still be a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each proposed move, verify that every character matches a known Roman numeral or allowed operator shape.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may move sticks from an operator without ensuring the resulting shape corresponds to a permitted operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When altering an operator, check that the new configuration matches exactly one of the allowed operator symbols.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes tries random stick moves without first quantifying how far the left and right sides differ, leading to ineffective changes.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Start by converting the Roman numerals to integers and compute the difference; use this as a guide for which values need to increase or decrease.
